extracted.intended_audience: students and critics of literature; readers studying the novel
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative criteria for reading, analyzing, and producing novels emphasizing the "prophetic" mode and the aesthetic notion of pattern/rhythm. Focuses on how voice, character-extension, realism, depiction of evil, and structural pattern contribute to a novel's artistic effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Humility and absence of sense of humour in prophetic fiction
rubrics_metrics.description: Prophetic fiction 'demands humility and the absence of the sense of humour.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The prophetic novelist asks readers to lay aside sniggering and single vision; humility is a precondition for receiving the prophetic song. Anti-pattern: reading prophetic passages irreverently or too amusedly, which dissipates their effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reaching back into universals / extension of character
rubrics_metrics.description: Prophetic characters 'reach back'—individuals (e.g., Mitya) connect us with all other people; characters may 'extend' into a region implied beyond ordinary fiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design characters so that, while they remain particular persons, they evoke sensations or states that link to broader human experience (pity, love, spiritual resonance). Example: Dostoevsky's Mitya whose 'good dream' invites readers to share something deeper than his experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spasmodic or intermittent realism
rubrics_metrics.description: Prophetic fiction is 'spasmodically realistic'—moments of patient accuracy about ordinary details (trials, staircases, catalogues) alternate with the prophetic song.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use vivid, concrete foreground detail intermittently to ground prophetic passages; this roughness of surface generates little cries of approval while the work is read and is forgotten later when the overall song remains. Anti-pattern: uniform mundane realism without those luminous interruptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: The prophetic voice: song rather than talk
rubrics_metrics.description: What matters in prophecy is 'the accent of his voice, his song.' The prophet 'does not reflect' or 'hammer away'—he sings; whereas other novelists may be talkative, reflective, or workmanlike.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for a sustained tonal quality that feels like song—remote, concentrated, emotionally intense—rather than expository philosophizing or relentless analytic argument. Anti-pattern: Joyce-style workmanlike undermining where everything is explained and tightened by deliberation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confusion as incidental (prophecy) vs fundamental (fantasy)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prophecy's confusion is incidental, while fantasy's confusion is fundamental ('fantasy glances about... fantasy's [confusion] is fundamental').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If employing prophetic techniques, allow incidental bewilderment to enrich the song without making incoherence the method itself. In fantasy, changing mythologies and radical structural play are intrinsic; do not conflate the two approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prophet composes from a remoter emotional state
rubrics_metrics.description: The prophet composes 'more completely than the fantasist' and 'is in a remoter emotional state while he composes.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage an authorial stance that feels as if working from a heightened, distanced emotion—not merely recounting experience but evoking a transpersonal sensation. This tone distinguishes prophetic writing from incidental or quotidian narration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characters can be flat yet extend to round when action requires it
rubrics_metrics.description: Flat characters may 'become... round when the action required it'—they can extend when needed; conversely a round character (e.g., Mitya) can still be 'capable of extension.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design characters with potential elasticity: allow apparently flat figures to expand in key moments, and permit rounded figures to resonate beyond themselves. Anti-pattern: rigidly fixed flatness that never serves a larger effect, or roundness that never connects outward.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid turning objects/incidents into rigid symbols that silence the book
rubrics_metrics.description: It is 'wrong to turn the Delight or the coffin into symbols, because even if the symbolism is correct, it silences the book.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use symbolic elements subtly; resist over-formalizing incidental motifs into fixed allegories that explain away the book's roughness and song. Keep ambiguity and unformulated connections where they enrich the prophetic effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depict evil as transcendent contest rather than mere plot device
rubrics_metrics.description: Melville conceives evil as a contest; evil is not merely sexual/social misconduct or a convenient villain—it can be envisaged as a transcending blackness or force.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When portraying evil, aim for grandeur and universality (as in Moby Dick or Billy Budd) rather than petty villainy that serves only to advance plot; avoid villains who are merely mercenary or sordid—real villainy in this mode is serious, proud, and unsensational.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of isolated episodes to illuminate larger prophetic mind
rubrics_metrics.description: Remote, unearthly episodes (e.g., Billy Budd, the sermon about Jonah) function as songs that throw light on the author's larger conception.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include concentrated episodes that are themselves self-contained songs or parables; they should illuminate the novel's central apprehensions without needing didactic exposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Roughness of surface as a virtue
rubrics_metrics.description: Prophetic works show 'roughness of surface'—dents, grooves, lumps and spikes that provoke immediate responses but are later forgotten when the work's song remains.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow irregularities, digressions, and textural roughness to survive in the published work; these features can heighten the prophetic music of the whole. Anti-pattern: over-smoothing the text so that the prophetic quality is lost.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pattern as an aesthetic aspect of the novel
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Pattern' is an aesthetic aspect that lets the reader 'see the book as a whole'—a pictorial or geometrical shape (hour-glass, grand chain) summing up structural symmetry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider the novel's overall shape and how characters/incidents form visual or structural patterns. Examples: Thais as an hour-glass (two characters converge and cross), Roman Pictures as a grand chain (characters hand the narrator on through society). The pattern provides a kind of aesthetic pleasure beyond plot curiosity or intellectual understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pattern springs mainly from plot and draws nourishment from it
rubrics_metrics.description: Pattern 'springs mainly out of the plot' and 'draws most of its nourishment from the plot.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When aiming for pattern, design plots whose sequence and relations naturally produce the intended shape; the plot's neat carpentry can found the pattern and allow beauty to emerge. Anti-pattern: forcing a pattern that contradicts or undermines the organic plot.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pattern must suit the author's mood and be appropriate to tone
rubrics_metrics.description: The value of a pattern lies in 'the suitability of the pattern to the author's mood' (Roman Pictures' pattern suits Lubbock's comic, sub-acid mood).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Match structural patterns to the work's atmosphere and tone; select shapes (symmetry, chain, cyclical forms) that amplify the author's predisposed aesthetic rather than impose an alien design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pattern externalizes atmosphere and provides unity
rubrics_metrics.description: Pattern 'externalizes' atmosphere and binds scattered incidents together with a thread 'woven out of their own substance'; it causes us to perceive the book as a whole and provides unity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use recurring structural movements or symmetrical arrangements to turn diffuse atmosphere into perceivable form, so that the ending feels pre-arranged and satisfying. Anti-pattern: atmospheric effects that never cohere into an overarching pattern.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pattern often requires pre-arrangement and sacrifice of other elements
rubrics_metrics.description: For pattern to 'triumph' an author may make sacrifices—everything must be planned and fit; minor characters must not be mere decoration but must 'elaborate on the main theme.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be willing to limit or shape incidental material so it serves the pattern. Ensure minor characters and episodes actively contribute to the central structural symmetry. Anti-pattern: including colorful but irrelevant material that distracts from the unified pattern.

rubrics_metrics.name: Symmetry and role-exchange as pattern devices (hour-glass)
rubrics_metrics.description: Patterns like the hour-glass rely on symmetry and exchange of roles (e.g., Thais: Paphnuce and Thais converge, cross, and recede; The Ambassadors: Strether and Chad change places).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ mirrored trajectories, role reversals, or convergences to create memorable structural shapes. Make sure the shifts are motivated and discernible so the reader can experience the formal pleasure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minor characters should elaborate the main theme, not merely decorate
rubrics_metrics.description: In pattern-rich novels 'none of the minor characters are just decorative... they elaborate on the main theme, they work.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Craft secondary figures to reinforce thematic or structural concerns—use them to extend the pattern, deepen atmosphere, or clarify contrasts. Anti-pattern: inert extras who add surface color but nothing to the pattern.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pattern produces a pleasure without explicit explanation
rubrics_metrics.description: Pattern 'causes us to see the book as a whole' and produces 'a pleasure without knowing why.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accept that pattern can elicit an aesthetic response not wholly analyzable; design for that emergent pleasure while ensuring structural coherence. Use geometrical or pictorial metaphors post hoc to help explanation, but do not over-explain during composition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish pattern from rhythm
rubrics_metrics.description: When the unity of the book is not the main aesthetic shape we should call the recurring aesthetic quality 'rhythm' rather than pattern.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the book's beauty arises from recurring motifs, beats, or pacing rather than a single overall shape, treat and craft it as rhythm—borrow musical terms and think in repetitions and cycles rather than one-off symmetry.
